title: Understanding the role of lipids in structure and function of membrane proteins
text:
Membrane proteins are embedded in the complex lipid environment of the biological membrane. Membrane
protein function is often regulated by specific lipid interactions and, therefore, the identification and
characterization of protein-lipid interactions is of paramount biological importance. This proposal seeks to apply
highly innovative and integrative approaches, combining numerous biophysical techniques, to identify and
characterize protein-lipid interactions at the molecular level.

title: Systematic modeling and prediction of cell-type-specific and spatiotemporal crosstalk pathways in Alzheimer's Disease
text:
For last two decades, Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) research has been focusing on a neuron-centric biochemical
process that leads to synaptic deficits and neuronal degeneration. However, recent failures in clinical trials call
for studies that lead to unbiased and holistic understanding of disease pathways in different types of brain
cells. This project aims to unbiasedly explore and validate neuron-glia and glia-glia interaction in the AD brain
by combining a computational systems biology platform, novel 3D Alzheimer’s-in-a-dish models, and the
enriched multiple-omics AD databases. The completion of this study will provide a validated integrated
bioinformatics tool to unbiasedly identify altered neuron-glia and glia-glia crosstalk pathways in AD and will
provide novel therapeutic targets and repositioned drug candidates for translating into clinical studies for AD
patients.

title: Testing Hypothesized Pathways Linking Infection, Physical Activity, Apoe Genotype, And Biological Sex To Low Dementia Prevalence And Reduced Brain Atrophy In Two Native American Populations
text:
This research will investigate the risk of cognitive impairment, dementia and brain atrophy in relation to
physical activity, infection and immune pathways, biological sex, and APOE genotype among two cohorts of
Native Americans whose lifestyle and environment require high levels of physical activity and expose them to
high pathogen burdens, most like the human preindustrial past. The study extends on-going research that has
revealed a very low prevalence of dementia, especially Alzheimer’s disease, but a high level of arterial
calcification in the brain associated with mild cognitive impairment. These populations offer a vanishing
opportunity to study how risk factors operate in diverse environments, assess the role of infection in AD and
brain aging, and generate a biobank for future research and access to data-sharing consortia.

title: 3D MRI Method for CMRO2 Mapping of the Brain in Dementia
text:
Alzheimer’s disease, which affects nearly seven million Americans, is known to be related to defective brain
oxygen metabolism. The proposed magnetic resonance imaging technology, which is able to provide new insight
into brain energetics, can readily be integrated into standard MRI scanners and is projected to allow evaluation
of the disease and serve as a means for assessing the effectiveness of treatment.

title: Deltaretrovirus Morphology and Particle Assembly
text:
Deltaretroviruses are complex retroviruses, are associated with the development of lymphoid leukemias, and are
notorious for being difficult to propagate in cell culture, which has prohibited rigorous analyses of virus replication,
including the steps involved in retrovirus assembly. Deltaretroviruses have distinct immature and mature particle
morphologies and utilize a distinct pathway for particle biogenesis. The studies proposed in this application will
advance knowledge regarding the novel aspects of deltaretrovirus assembly, which will expand fundamental
knowledge of retrovirus assembly and help reveal novel therapeutic targets for antiviral intervention.

title: Deciphering the role of the novel long non-coding RNA LINC01896 in glioblastoma multiforme
text:
This study will define the oncogenic role of the long non-coding RNA LINC01896 in glioblastoma
(GBM) initiation and progression. By elucidating its regulatory function, we will gain critical insights
into GBM pathogenesis. These findings could pave the way for novel targeted therapeutic
strategies, ultimately advancing treatment approaches for high-grade brain tumors.

title: Generating functional diversity from molecular homogeneity at glutamatergic synapses
text:
Synapses are the primary substrates driving information transfer throughout our nervous system.
Defects in synaptic communication are associated with a vast number of neurological,
neurodegenerative, and neuropsychiatric diseases including epilepsy, autism, schizophrenia,
ALS, and Alzheimer’s Disease. While their importance is undeniable, the mechanisms that
establish and modulate the diversity of synaptic strength remain enigmatic. This proposal seeks
to reveal fundamental insights into what determines and adaptively modifies the diversity of
presynaptic function at glutamatergic synapses in development and plasticity. Ultimately, this
knowledge is necessary to understand the etiology of neural diseases resulting from synaptic
dysfunction and develop effective therapeutic strategies.

title: Study of the Cellular Basis of Herpes Simplex Encephalitis with hPSC-Derived CNS and PNS Cells
text:
In about 10% of children, forebrain HSE results from inborn errors of IFN-I-dependent or -independent antiviral
immunity, whereas brainstem HSE results from inborn errors of the RNA lariat debranching enzyme DBR1. We
aim to study the CNS-, tissue-, and cell-intrinsic basis of forebrain and brainstem HSE, using patient-specific
hPSC-derived forebrain and hindbrain neurons and organoids, or microglial cells, or both, in two-dimensional
culture and organoid models. These studies will enable us to analyze in greater depth and breadth the cellular
basis of human CNS-intrinsic immunity to HSV-1 and the pathogenesis of HSE, a life-threatening, not so rare,
and isolated viral infection of the human brain.

title: Mechanism of ketogenic diet-induced hypercholesterolemia
text:
Management of hypercholesterolemia to reduce atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease risk is central to
preventive cardiology, and ketogenic diets can cause profound hypercholesterolemia despite other therapeutic
benefits. Accomplishment of the research aims will clarify the mechanism of ketogenic diet-induced
hypercholesterolemia in susceptible adults, which will have clinical implications for the care of patients with this
lipid disorder and will also yield basic insights into human lipid, lipoprotein, and ketone metabolism. This
Career Development Award will launch the candidate’s independent career in mechanistic clinical investigation
of ketone and lipid metabolism in cardiometabolic health and disease.

title: Integrated therapies for alcohol use and ALD (ITAALD) Network – UTSW Clinical Center
text:
:
Alcohol-associated liver disease (ALD) is a leading cause of mortality/morbidity, and there is no FDA-approved therapy for any stage of ALD. Unfortunately, patients with ALD rarely have their underlying alcohol use disorder (AUD) concomitantly addressed. This consortium links health providers with expertise in AUD and ALD in a unified treatment strategy to evaluate novel combined treatments for AUD/ALD in patients with advanced ALD. The exiting resources of the NIAAA-funded consortium are used for patient studies, biospecimen collection and site-specific translational studies.

title: Divergent response to radio-immunotherapy in HNSCC and PDAC is mediated by regulatory T cells
text:
Head and neck cancer (HNSCC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) exhibit dichotomous
responses to combination radiation immunotherapy in the context of OX40 agonism, highlighted by decreased
CD8 T cell effector function and enhanced regulatory T cell (Treg) suppression, resulting in diminished survival
in PDAC models. The PDAC tumor microenvironment (TME) is rich in IL-33 and Tregs which express the
cognate receptor ST2. We aim to determine the differential responses to OX40 agonism between HNSCC and
PDAC, and whether the IL-33/ST2 axis on Tregs promotes a suppressive TME.

title: HIV-1 Fusion Peptide-directed Vaccine Design Using Virus-like Particles
text:
There is an unmet need in the HIV vaccine field for immunogens that consistently elicit potent and broad
neutralizing antibodies. We have developed HIV-1 fusion peptide immunogens using alphavirus-like particles
which, when combined with Env trimer boosts, consistently elicited cross-clade neutralizing antibodies in nearly
all immunized subjects. We aim to further enhance serum cross-neutralizing titers with next-generation virus-like
particle and Env trimer immunogens.

title: Role of Peripheral Inflammation in TBI Pathobiology
text:
Traumatic brain injury (TBI) remains a public health concern, the consequences of which can lead to long-lasting
disability and cognitive dysfunction. Inflammation after TBI can serve both beneficial and detrimental roles, with
uncontrolled inflammation profoundly influencing neuronal survival and outcome. The present proposal will
investigate the role of the neuropeptide CART (cocaine and amphetamine regulated transcript) in the regulation
of inflammation after TBI, and if this neuropeptide can be used to reduce TBI pathophysiology and improve
cognitive outcome.

title: University of Utah Core Vision Research Grant
text:
Vision research spans a vast range of basic science areas (cell biology, molecular biology, neurobiology,
chemistry, biochemistry, computer science, human and mouse genetics, optics, physiology) with strong
traditional links to neuroscience and newly evolving dimensions in translational research on ocular diseases.
The principle underlying the Vision Research Core (VRC) at the University of Utah is that research excellence
is best served by ready access to resources outside the scope of individual R01 awards, ready access to
technical expertise outside the scope a single laboratory, and staff training to remove barriers to efficient
translational research and collaboration.

title: Dopamine receptor type 2 (D2)-expressing cells in the ventral hippocampus controlrelapse behavior
text:
Substance use disorders (SUDs) are a major public health concern given that up to 10% of United
States adults will suffer from SUDs at some point in their life, yet there are currently no FDA-approved
treatments for many SUDs to drugs of abuse like cocaine. This proposal characterizes dopamine
receptor type 2 (D2)-expressing cells within the ventral hippocampus (vHPC) as a novel potential
therapeutic target implicated in relapse vulnerability. Using a combination of drug self-administration,
one-photon calcium imaging, machine learning, RNA-sequencing, and electrophysiology, these data
will lead to a better understanding of how drugs of abuse hijack mesocorticolimbic circuitry to facilitate
maladaptive reward processing and augmented drug seeking and taking behavior, ultimately revealing
novel cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying relapse and potential therapeutic targets to
improve treatments outcomes for cocaine use disorder.

title: Addressing Disparities in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: Utilization of Health-Related Social Needs and Predictive Analytics to Improve Clinical Outcomes
text:
Dr. Abbott’s K08 research project addresses critical gaps and known disparities in out-of-hospital cardiac
arrest (OHCA) clinical outcomes and survival through the development and testing of enhanced predictive
models that include pre-hospital, patient-level, hospital-level and individual-level health-related social needs
(HRSN) data. Using natural language processing (NLP) and large language models (LLMs), mediation
analysis, and machine learning algorithms, his study will advance current predictive models improving clinical
care and survival for OHCA patients. His research will result not only in important knowledge and techniques
regarding the inclusion of HRSN for OHCA care, but also set the stage for his subsequent R01-supported
study to externally validate in other health systems the HRSN-inclusive models from this K08 research project.

title: Engineered Asymmetric Hydrogel for Muscle Stem Cell Polarity and Fate Specification
text:
Skeletal muscle stem cell transplantation is emerging as a promising strategy for treating muscle-associated
trauma and disorders, but the paucity in their quantity limits their therapeutic potential. The inability to maintain
and expand these cells ex vivo further compounds this challenge. This research will develop a geometrically
asymmetric culture platform that enable long-term maintenance and expansion of muscle stem cells by
directing cellular polarity, division, and fate determination.

title: Molecular Mechanisms of Human Meningomyelocele (Spina Bifida)
text:
This project will expand on preliminary data to achieve a comprehensive assessment of the genetic contributions
to human meningomyelocele (MM) through targeted recruitment, genetic assessment, linked environmental folic
acid exposure and clinical context, with the goal of developing better prevention strategies.

title: Molecular Chemiluminescence Probes for Imaging of Amyloid beta in Animal Models
text:
In preclinical therapeutic studies, the ability to conduct high-throughput imaging of large quantities of mice is
crucial. While bioluminescence imaging has been widely utilized in cancer drug discovery and offers high-
throughput capabilities, it is not readily applicable to Alzheimer's disease (AD) research. However,
chemiluminescence imaging, similar to bioluminescence imaging, possesses desirable features such as high
signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs), cost-effectiveness, and the potential for high-throughput imaging. In this proposal,
we hypothesize that the chemiluminescence probe ADLumin-X can be effectively employed to monitor the
therapeutic effects of AD drugs using a high-throughput approach in AD mouse models. By leveraging the
advantageous properties of chemiluminescence imaging, we aim to facilitate an efficient and comprehensive
evaluation of the efficacy of AD therapeutics in a large number of mice. By employing ADLumin-X as a tool for
high-throughput chemiluminescence imaging, we anticipate significant advancements in our ability to monitor
and assess the therapeutic responses of AD mice. This approach can potentially enhance the efficiency and
effectiveness of AD drug discovery and evaluation processes, ultimately leading to improved treatments for AD.

title: Children's Research Institute Hematology Research Training Grant
text:
The Pediatric Hematology and Transfusion Medicine Multidisciplinary Research Training Award (PHTMMRT) at
Children's National is a rigorous 2- to 3-year mentored program of career development and research training for
post-doctoral pediatric subspeciality trainees who have demonstrated potential for and interest in pursuing
research careers particularly in the areas of red cell biology, and sickle cell disease, cell
therapies/immunobiology, infection/inflammation and coagulation/vascular biology. The ultimate goal of
PHTMMRT is to develop independent clinician-investigators and academic leaders in the scientific domains of
relevance to The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute.
